title: Mirror task code in random intrinsic subspace
hypothesis: On task updates expressed in a shared low-dimensional intrinsic subspace, a shared code vector plus task-specific Givens angle can reduce stored task coordinates while retaining query quality; independent random-subspace tuning and generic PCA are mandatory controls.
physical_object: frozen random projection U from D=128 to intrinsic dimension d=16
mirror_coordinate: one shared intrinsic vector z plus one per-task Givens angle
logical_multiplicity: eight linear task functions per world
controls: independent coefficients in the same frozen random intrinsic subspace (PA33)
shared Mirror orbit code learned jointly
generic rank-2 PCA over independently fitted intrinsic task vectors

development.selection_metric: fresh-independent support and query NRMSE, actual serialized bytes, fit updates and wall time

paid_objects: independent intrinsic task coordinates or shared Mirror z and angles

success_gate: Aligned stratum query NRMSE <=0.05 with at least 20% fewer total payload bytes than independent intrinsic coordinates; Mirror-specific claim requires better quality-per-byte than generic rank-2 PCA. Independent stratum must document private-capacity boundary.
failure_gate: Mirror misses quality on aligned tasks or fails to reduce bytes; generic PCA matching Mirror means no Mirror-specific advantage. Independent tasks are not a Mirror failure if they show the predeclared boundary.
boundaries: U is a random frozen projection, not a pretrained model
Aligned stratum is teacher-generated from the Givens orbit
No language model or natural task claim
